title: Word Search II
prompt:
Given an `m x n` board of letters and a list of `words`, return every word that can be spelled by a path of horizontally or vertically adjacent cells. A cell may not be used twice within one word. Return the words in any order.

**Example**: board `[["o","a","a","n"],["e","t","a","e"],["i","h","k","r"],["i","f","l","v"]]`, words `["oath","pea","eat","rain"]` → `["oath","eat"]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ m, n ≤ 12; up to 3·10⁴ distinct words, each 1–10 lowercase letters.

tests.note: would need to reuse a cell
found from two cells, reported once

hints: Running Word Search separately for each of thousands of words repeats the same prefix exploration over and over. How could all the words share their common prefixes?
Put every word into a trie, then backtrack from each cell once, moving down the trie with each letter. Stop as soon as the trie has no child for the current letter.
Store the full word at its end node. When you reach it, add it and set `node.word = null` so it can't be added twice. Mark a cell `'#'` before exploring its neighbours and restore it afterwards.

solution.explanation: The trie merges all the words into one prefix tree, so a single backtracking search per starting cell looks for every word at once and stops the moment the current path isn't a prefix of any word. Clearing `word` after a hit removes duplicates. Worst case O(m·n·4·3^(L−1)) for maximum word length L, but pruning keeps it far lower in practice; O(total word characters) space for the trie.
